items.s: Streaming picks for your Week 8 lineup, Sean Payton's plans for more Jonah Coleman, less J.K. Dobbins.

items.h: Fantasy football buzz: Starters on bye? Finish your lineup with these streamers
items.s: Streaming picks for your Week 8 lineup at quarterback, running back, wide receiver and tight end.

items.h: Two catches in loss
items.s: Bateman caught two of four targets for 33 yards during Sunday's 35-13 loss to the Bengals. Bateman was able to handle a full workload for the first time since Week 5 after dealing with a shoulder injury, and the wide receiver was on the field for 74 percent of the team's offensive snaps. Bateman finished tied for third on the team in targets with running back Justice Hill and tight end Mark Andrews, and his 33 receiving yards ranked third. The wide receiver and the rest of the team's pass catchers would stand to see an increase in production if Lamar Jackson (ankle) is able to return to action in Week 8 versus Buffalo.

items.h: Rashod Bateman hauls in two passes in Week 7
items.s: Rashod Bateman caught 2-of-4 targets for 33 yards in a 35-13 loss to the Bengals. Bateman has seen his role decrease over the last two weeks with the return of Ja'Kobi Lane to the lineup. Bateman is a bench stash at best right now for fantasy managers heading into a Week 8 matchup with the Bills.

items.h: Rashod Bateman a Bench Stash Against the Bengals
items.s: Baltimore Ravens wide receiver Rashod Bateman (shoulder) logged two full practices in a row and is good to go for Week 7 against the Cincinnati Bengals. Bateman has had two good games and four quiet games so far this season, and has been mostly dependent on injuries to his fellow receivers to get more opportunity. His best game of the season came in Week 2 when Zay Flowers was out, putting up seven catches for 88 yards and a touchdown against the New Orleans Saints. He also managed five receptions for 62 yards in Week 5, but with rookie Ja'Kobi Lane getting eased into the lineup after returning from injury, Bateman played just 30% of snaps last week. While a Lamar Jackson return does boost…

items.h: Rashod Bateman (shoulder) good to go for Sunday
items.s: Rashod Bateman (shoulder) is good to go for Sunday's game against the Cincinnati Bengals. Bateman will be good to go for Sunday's game after being limited by a shoulder issue earlier in the week. He isn't expected to be a trustworthy fantasy option in this game, however, though his ceiling will be raised considerably if QB Lamar Jackson (ankle) is cleared to play ahead of game time.

items.h: Free of restrictions in Thursday's practice
items.s: Bateman (shoulder) was a full participant in Thursday's practice. A limited practice participant to begin the week after he exited this past Sunday's loss to the Browns due to the shoulder issue, Bateman cleared up any concern about his health by taking every rep during Thursday's session. While he'll be ready to play Sunday versus the Bengals, Bateman's standing as the No. 2 wideout on the depth chart behind Zay Flowers could be threatened after rookie Ja'Kobi Lane produced well in his return from injured reserve last week, logging four catches for 40 yards on five targets.

items.h: Rashod Bateman (shoulder) limited at practice Wednesday
items.s: Rashod Bateman (shoulder) was limited at practice on Wednesday. Bateman is dealing with a shoulder issue right now. The exact severity of it is unknown, but he was able to practice in a limited fashion on Wednesday, so it appears to be more of a short-term issue. Rookie Ja'Kobi Lane will see more work in Week 7 if the veteran is unable to suit up.

items.h: Turns in limited practice
items.s: Bateman (shoulder) was a limited practice participant Wednesday. Per Jonas Shaffer of TheBaltimoreBanner.com, Bateman was sporting a no-contact jersey during the session, but his presence on the field in any capacity was a promising sign after he was unable to return to Sunday's 13-10 loss to the Browns. If he's able to take contact in practice at some point over the next two days, Bateman should be in good shape to play this weekend against the Bengals.

items.h: Practicing Wednesday
items.s: Bateman (shoulder) is taking part in Wednesday's practice, Brian Wacker of The Baltimore Sun reports. Bateman sustained a shoulder injury during this past Sunday's loss at Cleveland and wasn't able to return. Head coach Jesse Minter told Jeff Zrebiec of The Athletic on Monday that Bateman "should be OK," and the wide receiver's ability to mix into drills only days after the incident indicates he's trending in the right direction. Wednesday's practice report will reveal Bateman's activity level to begin Week 7 prep.

items.h: Rashod Bateman (shoulder) hopeful to be fine
items.s: Ravens coach Jesse Minter said there's optimism that Rashod Bateman will "be fine." Bateman remains off the fantasy radar when he is healthy.

items.h: Should be OK after exiting Week 6 loss
items.s: Ravens head coach Jesse Minter said Monday that Bateman (shoulder) "should be OK" after exiting late in the second quarter of Sunday's 13-10 loss to the Browns, Jeff Zrebiec of The Athletic reports. Listed on Ravens injury reports the past two weeks due to a shoulder issue, Bateman appeared to aggravate the injury late in the first half of Sunday's contest. He failed to haul in his lone target while running 11 routes in the game before the injury kept him out for the entire second half. Fortunately for Bateman, he seems to have avoided a major setback, but his practice activity over the next few days will likely determine whether he suits up next Sunday versus the Bengals. It's also worth…

items.h: Bateman (shoulder) has been ruled out of Sunday's game in Cleveland.
items.s: Bateman appears to have aggravated the shoulder injury that bothered him during Week 6 prep. Now that it's confirmed Bateman won't return Sunday, he'll finish the contest with no catches (on one target). Ja'Kobi Lane, Devontez Walker and LaJohntay Wester are the Ravens' available wide receivers behind top option Zay Flowers.

items.h: Bateman sustained a shoulder injury during Sunday's game at Cleveland, Brian Wacker of The Baltimore Sun reports.
items.s: Bateman tended to a shoulder injury during Week 6 prep, as he logged an LP/DNP/FP practice regimen. His listing Sunday indicates he aggravated the issue, which has left him questionable to return. Bateman didn't haul in his only target before exiting late in the first half.

items.h: Bateman (shoulder) doesn't have an injury designation for Sunday's game at Cleveland.
items.s: A full practice Friday erases the concern about Bateman's shoulder injury, whereas QB Lamar Jackson (ankle) still isn't practicing and won't play this week.

items.h: Bateman (shoulder) didn't practice Thursday.
items.s: Head coach Jesse Minter told Jamison Hensley of ESPN.com on Wednesday that Bateman "should be fine" for Sunday's game against the Browns, but it's unclear if the Ravens remain as confident in the wideout's health a day later. After opening Week 6 prep as a limited participant, Bateman took a step back in terms of activity Thursday. As long as he can get back on the field in some capacity Friday, Bateman will be in good shape to play this weekend, but another missed practice will put him at risk of missing his first game of the season.

items.h: Bateman (shoulder) was a limited participant in Wednesday's practice.
items.s: Per Cordell Woodland of 105.7 The Fan Baltimore, Bateman was spotted with a non-contact jersey Wednesday and was able to fit in some on-field work behind closed doors after not working out with the team during the open portion of the session. Though the wideout is on the injury report for a second straight week on account of the shoulder issue, head coach Jesse Minter said after Wednesday's practice that Bateman "should be fine" for Sunday's game against the Browns, according to Jamison Hensley of ESPN.com.

items.h: Bateman caught five of six passes for 62 yards during the Ravens' 30-23 overtime win over the Falcons on Sunday.
items.s: Bateman ended up leading the Ravens in receiving yards while finishing second in catches and targets to Zay Flowers (eight catches on nine targets). Bateman played a crucial role in Baltimore's come-from-behind victory, with the veteran wide receiver logging catches of 11, seven and 20 yards late in the fourth quarter (all for first downs), with the drive ending on a seven-yard touchdown pass from Tyler Huntley to Devontez Walker. Bateman has a 16-233-1 receiving line on 20 targets over his last four games, but his role on offense would likely decrease once rookie third-round wide receiver…

items.h: Bateman (shoulder) was a full participant in Thursday's practice.
items.s: According to Cordell Woodland of 105.7 The Fan Baltimore, Bateman was donning a red no-contact jersey during the open portion of Thursday's practice, but he was evidently able to do enough on the field to upgrade to full activity after a limited listing Wednesday. Though Bateman looks like he'll be ready to go for Sunday's game in Atlanta, he could be at the receiving end of passes from Tyler Huntley, who directed the first-team offense for a second straight day Thursday while starting quarterback Lamar Jackson (ankle) remained sidelined at practice. The Ravens likely will decide on…

items.h: Bateman (shoulder) was limited in Wednesday's practice.
items.s: It's a new injury for Bateman, and the same can be said for Zay Flowers, who was limited with a foot injury Wednesday. With Lamar Jackson (ankle) set to miss Week 5 against the Falcons, Bateman is an uninspiring fantasy bet if he plays.

items.h: Bateman caught both of his targets for 46 yards in Sunday's win over the Titans.
items.s: With Zay Flowers getting even closer to 100 percent with his hamstring injury and Mark Andrews and Derrick Henry seeing most of the money opportunities in the red zone, Bateman is left fighting for scraps. Bateman's days as a fantasy starter are likely over with Flowers nearing a full-time role, as the former has five targets over the last two games since Flowers' return.

items.h: Bateman caught two of three targets for 37 yards in Sunday's 34-31 win over the Cowboys.
items.s: Bateman finished second on the team in receiving yards behind Zay Flowers, who compiled 84 receiving yards in the latter's return from a one-game absence due to a hamstring injury. Bateman stepped up with seven catches for 88 yards and a touchdown while Flowers was sidelined in Week 2, but Flowers is the clear No. 1 option in Baltimore's wide receiver room, as Bateman was held without a catch when Flowers was active for the season opener. Up next for Bateman and the Ravens will be a Week 4 home game against the Titans.

items.s: Eric Karabell lists who he thinks are the top available players worth adding for the week ahead.

items.h: Week 2 winners and losers: Jaxon Smith-Njigba, CeeDee Lamb shine; Bijan Robinson struggles
items.s: Jaxon Smith-Njigba and CeeDee Lamb came up big in Week 2, while Bijan Robinson and Justin Jefferson had very quiet days.

items.h: Bateman caught seven of nine targets for 88 yards and a touchdown in Sunday's 24-17 loss to New Orleans.
items.s: With Zay Flowers (hamstring) unavailable, Bateman stepped up as Lamar Jackson's top downfield option and hauled in a 22-yard TD just before halftime, giving the Ravens a 14-3 lead. The veteran wideout made a mental error that may have cost his team the game, however -- on Baltimore's final possession as the Ravens were looking to tie it up, he cut a route short and saw Jackson's pass attempt sail over his head for a game-ending interception. Flowers could be back as soon as next week, which would relegate Bateman to a supporting role again for a Week 3 road trip to Dallas.

items.h: With teammate Zay Flowers (hamstring) listed as doubtful, Bateman has a big opportunity Sunday against the Saints, ESPN.com's Jamison Hensley reports.
items.s: Quarterback Lamar Jackson told reporters that Bateman "is actually going to get a lot more targets, I believe." The Ravens may not have any other choice after losing Flowers and Ja'Kobi Lane (IR - wrist) to injuries during a Week 1 win over Indianapolis. Bateman played 80 percent of Baltimore's snaps in the contest, including 85 percent before halftime when Flowers and Lane were still in the game. Bateman likely will handle another lofty snap share this Sunday, and his target rate may rise with Flowers' usual snaps/routes being split between lesser players like Devontez Walker, LaJohntay…

items.h: Bateman did not bring in his lone target during Baltimore's 41-23 win over Indianapolis on Sunday.
items.s: Bateman and Lamar Jackson connected on a 19-yard pass late in the second quarter, but that play was called back due to offensive holding. Jackson and Bateman failed to connect on a throw early in the third quarter, and the latter finished with zero catches for the fourth time since the beginning of the 2025 season. Bateman ended up leading all wide receivers with 53 offensive snaps, and despite the early dud, his role in the offense should expand for as long as rookie Ja'Kobi Lane is sidelined by a fractured wrist, and even more so if Zay Flowers (hamstring) were to miss time. The Ravens…

items.h: Fantasy football free agent pickups: Shough, Black, Coker highlight top options for Week 2
items.s: Eric Karabell lists who he thinks are the top available players worth adding for the week ahead.

items.h: Bateman is facing three charges stemming from a domestic incident in June, Jamison Hensley of ESPN.com reports.
items.s: The Ravens released a statement Friday: "We are aware of the situation involving Rashod and have been in direct communication with him. We notified the league office and have been cooperating throughout the process. As this is a pending legal matter, we will not have further comment." The NFL likely won't levy any sort of punishment on Bateman until the legal process plays itself out.

items.h: Bateman is in full uniform for Thursday's practice.
items.s: Bateman didn't take part in either of the Ravens' last two practices, but the team didn't disclose whether his absences were injury-related or part of a planned maintenance plan. Either way, Bateman will be back on the field Thursday, but it's unclear if the Ravens intend to have him suit up in Saturday's preseason opener versus the Eagles. While Bateman projects to head into Week 1 as a starter alongside No. 1 wideout Zay Flowers, rookie third-round pick Ja'Kobi Lane has generated considerable buzz during camp and could be a threat to poach reps in two-receiver sets as the season unfolds.

items.h: Bateman is absent from practice Wednesday for a second straight day, Brian Wacker of The Baltimore Sun reports.
items.s: No injury has been reported, so it is possible that Bateman's absence is related to a personal matter. With Baltimore's preseason opener coming up this Saturday against Philadelphia, the coaching staff may soon have an update on Bateman's status.

items.h: As the coming season approaches, Bateman is projected to start at WR for the Ravens alongside Zay Flowers, Clifton Brown of the team's official site reports.
items.s: Bateman is coming off a 2025 regular season in which his production was hampered by injuries and tapered off to 19 catches (on 38 targets) for 224 yards and two TDs in 13 games. Assuming improved health this year, the 2021 first-rounder -- who recorded a 45-756-9 receiving line in 17 regular-season contests in 2024 -- is a bounce-back candidate in new offensive coordinator Declan Doyle's attack. Next in line on Baltimore's WR depth chart beyond Flowers and Bateman are returnees Devontez Walker and LaJohntay Wester, as well as rookie draftees Ja'Kobi Lane and Elijah Sarratt.

items.h: Bateman (personal) has been away from the team during OTAs the past two weeks, Jamison Hensley of ESPN.com reports.
items.s: Bateman was present for the start of the offseason program last month, but he's now tending to a personal matter. "He's dealing with some personal things and so he hasn't been here for a little bit," new offensive coordinator Declan Doyle said Tuesday. "I'm excited for him to get back in here in and keep rolling." Despite a down 2025 season, Bateman is expected to get the first crack at WR2 duties under Doyle.

items.h: Bateman (illness) is participating in OTAs this week.
items.s: Bateman missed the Ravens' Week 18 regular-season finale last season due to an illness but is back to 100 percent health four-plus months later. After a career year in 2024, which saw Bateman catch 45 passes for 756 yards and nine touchdowns, the receiver missed four games in 2025 and saw his numbers experience a dramatic decline, even when he was healthy. Bateman finished last season with just 19 catches for 224 yards and two touchdowns on 38 targets. As the coming season approaches, Bateman will again have a chance to handle WR2 duties behind Zay Flowers, with returnees Devontez Walker and…

items.h: Bateman (illness) has been downgraded from questionable to out for Sunday's game against the Steelers.
items.s: Head coach John Harbaugh initially expressed optimism Friday that Bateman would be able to play in Sunday's pivotal AFC North tilt, but the fifth-year wideout will end up being sidelined after missing practice all week while battling through an illness. With Bateman sidelined, Lamar Jackson will lean more on Zay Flowers, DeAndre Hopkins, Devontez Walker, Tylan Wallace and tight ends Mark Andrews and Isaiah Likely in the passing game. Bateman will end the 2025 regular season with 19 catches (on 39 targets) for 224 yards and two touchdowns across 13 games. He'll aim to progress enough in his…

items.h: Bateman (illness) did not practice Friday and is officially listed as questionable for Sunday night's regular-season finale against the Steelers, though head coach john Harbaugh said he expects the starting wideout to…
items.s: Bateman has missed three straight practices due to a lingering ailment, and though Harbaugh has stated that the veteran wideout will likely suit up Week 18, his status may not be made official until roughly 90 minutes prior to Sunday's 8:20 p.m. ET kickoff. Lamar Jackson (back) has been cleared to return to action for Sunday's divisional matchup, in which the AFC North title will be on the line, but Bateman nonetheless remains a risky bet for production even if he's healthy. Across his last five regular-season appearances, Bateman has compiled just four catches for 40 scoreless receiving…

items.h: Bateman (illness) is not participating in the early portion of Friday's practice open to the media, Brian Wacker of The Baltimore Sun reports.
items.s: Bateman appears on track to miss all three of Baltimore's practice sessions ahead of Sunday's night's regular-season finale against the Steelers, which will determine the victor of the AFC North title. Given the significance of the divisional matchup, the Ravens may list Bateman as questionable even if he's indeed unable to practice in any capacity Friday in order to give him every opportunity to contribute on offense. DeAndre Hopkins and Devontez Walker will benefit from increased playing time if Bateman can't go.

items.h: Bateman (illness) wasn't present for practice Thursday, Jonas Shaffer of TheBaltimoreBanner.com reports.
items.s: Bateman missed Wednesday's session, so the wideout now has just one opportunity to participate in practice ahead of Sunday night's regular-season finale against the Steelers. With the AFC North title on the line, Bateman likely will do anything he can to be available for the contest, but he may need to work fully Friday in order to head into the weekend without an injury designation.

items.h: Bateman missed Wednesday's practice with an illness.
items.s: Bateman should have time to recover before Sunday night's game at Pittsburgh. If not, WRs DeAndre Hopkins and Devontez Walker will be the favorites to get more playing time.

items.h: Bateman had a seven-yard reception on one target in Saturday's win over the Packers.
items.s: Bateman continues to see a healthy snap share (53% in Week 17), but his target share remains limited. He has three catches for 30 yards on seven targets in four games since suffering an ankle injury in Week 10 that cost him two weeks. In fairness, Baltimore only asked Tyler Huntley to throw it 20 times in Saturday's win as it leaned heavily on Derrick Henry and the run game. The leading receiver, Zay Flowers, topped out with four catches for 30 yards. If Lamar Jackson (back) remains out or is limited in Week 18, there may not be much passing volume to go around for players like Bateman.

items.h: Bateman failed to reel in either of his two targets in Sunday night's 28-24 loss to the Patriots.
items.s: Bateman missed the previous game with an ankle injury but returned to his clear WR2 role behind Zay Flowers against New England. However, Bateman's two targets were three fewer than DeAndre Hopkins, despite Bateman out-snapping Hopkins 38 to 20. After an impressive 2024 season that saw Bateman post a 45-756-9 receiving line, he's caught more than two passes in a game just once this season with a total of two touchdowns.

items.h: Bateman (ankle) was a full participant in practice Wednesday.
items.s: Bateman is thus set to return for Sunday's matchup with New England, after missing the Week 15 win at Cincinnati. His availability leaves less playing time for fellow wideouts DeAndre Hopkins and Devontez Walker, neither of whom has done much with Bateman bothered by various injuries in the second half of the season.

items.h: Bateman (ankle) is participating in Wednesday's practice, Jeff Zrebiec of The Athletic reports.
items.s: Bateman will likely be limited Wednesday, but it's encouraging to see him back on the practice field after he missed Baltimore's win over the Bengals in Week 15. He was added to the injury report as limited last Thursday then missed practice entirely Friday. Bateman's production has been disappointing in 2025, as across 11 regular-season appearances he's tallied just 18 catches for 217 yards and two scores on 36 targets.

items.h: Bateman (ankle) is inactive for Sunday's game against the Bengals.
items.s: Bateman was added to the Ravens' Week 15 injury report after being a limited participant in Thursday's practice and then missing Friday's session before heading into the weekend listed as questionable for Sunday's contest. In his absence, DeAndre Hopkins, Tylan Wallace, Devontez Walker and LaJohntay Wester are candidates to log increased snaps behind top wide receiver Zay Flowers.

items.h: Bateman (ankle) is officially listed as questionable for Sunday's game against the Bengals.
items.s: Ravens coach John Harbaugh said Friday that Bateman is still "fighting through" a lingering ankle sprain, and that the team will make a decision about his availability on Saturday. If Bateman isn't able to suit up for Sunday's divisional matchup, all of DeAndre Hopkins, Tylan Wallace, Devontez Walker and LaJohntay Wester will be candidates to benefit from increased snaps behind top wide receiver Zay Flowers.

items.h: Bateman (ankle) wasn't spotted at practice Friday, Jamison Hensley of ESPN.com reports.
items.s: Bateman was added to the Ravens' Week 15 injury report after being deemed a limited participant in Thursday's practice. With the wideout not present for Friday's session, his status for Sunday's game against the Bengals is now cloudy. If he's unavailable this weekend, added WR snaps alongside Zay Flowers would be available for some combination of DeAndre Hopkins, Tylan Wallace, Devontez Walker and LaJohntay Wester.

items.h: Bateman (ankle) was a limited participant in Thursday's practice.
items.s: Bateman wasn't listed on Wednesday's injury report, but he's now having his on-field reps capped. The veteran wideout also began Week 14 as a full participant before downgrading to limited action mid-week, and he was then able to suit up versus Pittsburgh without being assigned an injury designation. Barring any setbacks, Bateman should manage to gain clearance for Sunday's matchup against the Bengals in similar fashion.

items.h: Bateman caught two of three targets for 23 yards Sunday against the Steelers.
items.s: Bateman, who missed two weeks with an ankle injury, was more involved Sunday than he was in his Week 13 return, and his snap count jumped from 44 to 69. It didn't translate to a major jump in usage though, as he still drew just three targets. His one target that went incomplete was a crucial third down in the red zone that ended a drive and forced Baltimore to settle for a field goal. Bateman's production has fallen off sharply from his career year in 2024 when he had 45 catches for 756 yards and nine touchdowns. Through 11 games, Bateman has 18 catches on 36 targets for 217 yards and two…

items.h: Bateman (ankle) doesn't have a designation for Sunday's contest versus the Steelers.
items.s: Bateman sandwiched full sessions around a limited practice Thursday due to a lingering ankle injury that sidelined him Weeks 11 and 12. In his return to action last Thursday against the Bengals, he logged a 73 percent snap share but was targeted only one time, which he couldn't corral. In 10 appearances overall this season, Bateman's 16-194-2 line on 33 targets hasn't afforded him much sway in the fantasy realm.

items.h: Bateman (ankle) was limited at practice Thursday.
items.s: Bateman worked fully Wednesday, but a limited session a day later makes the wideout's Week 14 status worth tracking for those who roster him in deeper formats. In the 10 games Bateman has played in this season, he's caught more than two passes only once, en route to compiling a 16-194-2 line on 32 targets.

items.h: Bateman finished without any receptions and logged just one target in Thursday's 32-14 loss to Cincinnati.
items.s: Bateman at least played 73 percent of snaps on offense, returning to his usual workload after missing the previous two games with an ankle injury. He's now at just 6.1 yards per target on the season, down from a career-high 10.5 YPT last year (with nine TDs on 72 targets). Bateman has taken a big step back along with the rest of Baltimore's offense, but there's no hint yet of losing the No. 2 WR job when healthy. Next up is a Week 14 home game against Pittsburgh.

items.h: Bateman (ankle) doesn't have an injury designation for Thursday's game against the Bengals.
items.s: The Ravens listed Bateman as a full practice participant Wednesday for the first time since he sprained his ankle back in Week 10. He'll return from a two-game absence to face one of the NFL's worst defenses, albeit on a cold night in Baltimore while playing for a Ravens offense that doesn't seem to have its usual spark.
